links.outcome: Whether validator finding counts reflect derivation correctness versus multiple evaluation methods
links.effect: Validator findings ranged from 15 to 64 dataset-rule pairs. The package with fewest findings had none of 234 efficacy summary records in specified form. CRITIC reduced findings in 4 of 4 usable workflows but no failed derivations.
links.quote: The package with the fewest findings carried none of the 234 efficacy summary records in the form the specifications define, showing that lower validator finding counts do not necessarily indicate more correct derivations.

unlisted_practices: Agent self-revision using its own validator report (CRITIC) for clinical trial dataset generation
Network-restricted containerized evaluation of coding agents to prevent access to reference outputs

screen.reason: The study introduces a benchmark (ClinDataBench) for LLM agents generating CDISC clinical trial data packages and explicitly tests deployment/operational practices (Base vs. Self-Refine vs. CRITIC using automated validator reports) to assess whether feedback/validation guardrails reduce errors.

primary.practice: automated validator feedback revision (CRITIC / self-refine guardrails)
